record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: For planar systems of the form ẋ = P_{2k+1}(x,y), ẏ = Q_{2ℓ+1}(x,y), where P_{2k+1} and Q_{2ℓ+1} are homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees 2k+1 and 2ℓ+1, determine the maximum possible number of oscillations of the period function for those systems that have a center.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. (ii) Which is the maximum number of oscillations of the period function for the centers of the above family?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar polynomial differential systems of the form
  ẋ = P_{2k+1}(x,y),   ẏ = Q_{2ℓ+1}(x,y),
where P_{2k+1} and Q_{2ℓ+1} are homogeneous polynomials in (x,y) of odd degrees 2k+1 and 2ℓ+1 respectively, with k, ℓ ≥ 0 integers. Assume that the origin is a center of such a system, so that it is surrounded by a punctured neighborhood (the period annulus) entirely foliated by periodic orbits. For each periodic orbit γ in the period annulus, let T(γ) denote its minimal period; parameterizing the orbits by a smooth transverse parameter s ∈ (0, s*), one obtains the period function s ↦ T(s). A "critical period" is an isolated critical point of T(s), and the number of oscillations of the period function is the number of such critical periods.

Determine the maximum possible number of oscillations of the period function, taken over all centers in the family of systems above (as a function of k and ℓ).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of bounding the number of critical periods (oscillations of the period function) for centers of planar polynomial systems with homogeneous odd-degree nonlinearities is part of an active research program. Partial results exist for specific subfamilies (e.g., generalized Loud-type families and low-degree cases), and uniform boundedness in terms of degree is conjectured, but no general formula or sharp maximum is established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The period function of generalized Loud's centers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the bifurcation diagram of the period function at the polycycle bounding the period annulus, determining parameter regions for monotonicity or at least one critical period.
status_evidence.claim: Results are partial and specific to subfamilies; the general maximum remains undetermined.

status_evidence.title: Criticality via first order development of the period constants
status_evidence.snippet: Develops tools to count critical periods via period constants for polynomial centers.
status_evidence.claim: Active methodology, but no closed form bound for general (2k+1,2ℓ+1) homogeneous families.
